title: context-aware-worklet-orchestrator
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a context-aware Worklet Orchestrator (WKO) that composes small, typed admin worklets into safe, executable remediation flows for first-line support. The goal is to let oncall and support engineers assemble runbook fragments (worklets) at runtime with automated RBAC checks, dry-run simulation, and an idempotence guard. WKO should surface cost/latency impact and attach telemetry for every composed flow.
acceptance_criteria: Support assembling at least 5 worklet types into a single flow via Console UI and CLI
Dry-run simulator executes synthetic inputs with no side-effects and produces telemetry trace
RBAC checks block any flow that requires escalation and present escalation path
Flows are annotated with estimated token and GPU cost and per-step latency estimates
Worklet executions include an idempotence header and automatic retry/backoff policy
Audit log entries created for every executed flow with linkable traces
plan: Design worklet schema with typed inputs, outputs, and preconditions (1 week)
Prototype dry-run simulator that replays worklet API calls against a sandbox environment (2 weeks)
Integrate RBAC gating and KMS-check for secrets usage (1 week)
Add telemetry hooks, tagging, and cost-estimation model (1 week)
Build Console surface for composing and launching flows with canary rollout (2 sprints)
Run security review and incident tabletop using WKO (pre-release)
updates: 2026-01-25: Kickoff meeting with PM, Design, and Security. Outcome: align on typed inputs and required audit fields.
2026-02-03: Prototype schema v0.1 implemented. Feedback from Design: require explicit failure-mode descriptions for each step.
2026-02-11: Dry-run simulator MVP can replay HTTP and db-mock actions against sandbox. Still missing condition checks and idempotence enforcement.
2026-02-25: Security review flagged KMS key usage and recommended HSM integration for vault-unwrap. Added dependency ENG-642000.
2026-03-02: Telemetry schema agreed — include trace_id, user_id, flow_hash, cost_estimate, and slo_flags. Planning to emit traces to ops-telemetry.{prod,sandbox}.
2026-03-09: UX study with two oncall engineers. They asked for suggested templates and a reversible 'preview-and-stash' feature. Adding follow-up task ENG-765432.
blockers: Sandbox environment lacks synthetic KV cache; blocks reliable dry-run of cache-invalidation worklets
Awaiting HSM/KMS integration ETA from infra (dependency ENG-642000)
risks: Over-automation: composing privileged worklets could enable human error at scale without robust simulation
Cost estimation model may underpredict for bursty LLM jobs leading to unexpected billing alerts
RBAC enforcement gaps could permit privilege escalation if preconditions are incomplete
qa_strategy: Stepwise QA: unit tests for schema validation, integration tests against sandbox, e2e dry-run with simulated incidents
Tabletop exercise with Support and Oncall teams before beta launch
Chaos-style tests: randomized sequence of worklets to verify idempotence and safety fences
rollout_strategy: Internal beta for Platform & Support teams only
Feature flag gated in Console per org with gradual ramp over 2 weeks
Auto-fallback to manual runbook when simulation confidence < threshold
notes: Design decision: prefer explicit typed inputs over freeform YAML to reduce runtime validation errors
Trade-off: limiting worklet parameter surface reduces flexibility but simplifies RBAC reasoning
Edge-case: nested worklet invocation — will initially disallow to avoid recursive side-effects
